text.p: European mobile phone power Nokia Oy said Tuesday a strong upturn in handsets helped its first-quarter profit race ahead by over 260 percent, boosting its confidence for further growth and profitability.

Reporting pretax profit up at 1.45 billion markka ($278.7 million) from 399 million ($77 million) in a weak year-ago period, Nokia said its net sales climbed sharply to 11.33 billion ($2.18 billion) from 7.93 billion ($1.52 billion). Earnings per share were up to 3.79 markka (73 cents) from 1.14 (22 cents).

The median of analysts' forecasts had been for a 1.26-billion-markka ($242 million), profit and Nokia's stock posted strong gains in Helsinki and in the United States. In consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange, its stock rose $4.25 to $62.
"It hit all the right buttons," said Neil Barton, analyst at Merrill Lynch in London. He said Nokia's revenue growth and its gross margin around 31 percent were excellent.
Nokia said its overall earnings were helped by a strong recovery in its mobile phones arm, which made a slight operating loss in the year-ago period.
Net sales of mobile phones rose nearly 60 percent to 6.15 billion markka ($1.18 billion), with telecommunications infrastructure sales advancing over 34 percent to 3.73 billion ($717 billion).
"Our first-quarter results give us further confidence in our previously stated positive outlook for strong growth and good profitability for 1997," CEO Jorma Ollila said in a statement.

He told Reuters Financial Television that Nokia had reached its target 10 percent margin in mobile phone sales in the first quarter and said handset price erosion had continued, but Nokia had "more than matched" it.
